sections.section: Diffusion Art or Digital Forgery? Investigating Data Replication in Diffusion Models (p. 1–17)

omissions.source: The level of image similarity required for something to count as 'replication' is subjective... Rather than choosing an arbitrary definition, we focus on presenting quantitative and qualitative results to the reader, leaving each person to draw their own conclusions
the samples in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 are not cherry-picked, but they are chosen from the small subset of 20 images with highest top-1 similarity to the training data
these models can produce novel images of known identities from the training data without making verbatim copies

distortions.source: Feng et al. [24] study the conditions that lead GANs to replicate training data. They look for copies in pixel-space and find that such replications are inversely proportional to dataset complexity and dataset size.
distortions.summary: Related GAN studies (Meehan et al., Feng et al., Webster et al.) found replication inversely proportional to dataset complexity/size

distortions.source: Examples certainly exist of content replication from sources outside the 12M LAION Aesthetics v2 6+ split see Fig 12
distortions.summary: (e.g., 'The Scream' by Edvard Munch was generated from an image in the 600M Aesthetics 5+ split outside the searched 12M split)
